open_points.subject: Mapped-node output disclosure class at run time
open_points.text: A07 rule 3: "a function output [takes] the highest class its execution actually received"; A13 rule 6: "A mapped node... outputs are then lists in element order."
open_points.question: When a mapped node's elements receive different disclosure classes, what disclosure_class is assigned to the single aggregated list output value that downstream nodes receive?
options: Use the maximum class over all element executions for that mapped output list
Use each element's class separately (no single class on the aggregated list)
Use the class computed at proof time (maximum class that can reach any input) regardless of actual element classes
open_points.default_guess: Use the maximum class over all element executions for the aggregated list output.

open_points.subject: Recovery of in-flight effect attempt without persisted NodeExecution
open_points.text: A11 rule 1: "every attempt has exactly one concluding NodeExecution" and non-read sends write EffectAttempt `in_flight` before sending; A11 rule 4: "On start, every EffectAttempt still `in_flight` becomes `unknown` and its element waits as in rule 2"; rule 2 says the element's NodeExecution records `outcome_unknown`.
open_points.question: If the kernel crashes after writing `in_flight` but before writing any NodeExecution, does restart have to synthesize a NodeExecution `outcome_unknown` for that attempt, and if so with what timing/detail fields?
options: On restart, always create the missing NodeExecution `outcome_unknown` for that attempt number
Allow waiting based only on EffectAttempt and create no NodeExecution until later
Create NodeExecution only when the owner resolves the unknown outcome
open_points.default_guess: Create the missing NodeExecution `outcome_unknown` during startup recovery for the same attempt number.

open_points.subject: Owner access to spooled file bytes via inspection
open_points.text: A10 rule 2: "The owner may read the spooled file's bytes through inspection while the run holds them; an agent may not."
open_points.question: Which inspect operation returns raw spooled bytes, under what request shape and size/paging limits, and what exact refusal occurs after spool cleanup or release?
options: Define a dedicated inspect/read-file operation returning bytes with explicit size limits
Embed bytes in existing inspect run/trace responses
Allow only metadata in inspect and remove byte-reading despite this sentence
open_points.default_guess: Provide a dedicated owner-only read-spooled-file inspection path with bounded byte responses and refusal once spool is gone.
